meta.title: Mongolian B1 Intermediate
meta.subtitle: 1000 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Mongolian → English (see the Mongolian, recall the meaning) and English → Mongolian (see an English meaning, recall the Mongolian). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1000 words for an intermediate learner, aligned to B1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand the main points of clear standard input on familiar matters regularly encountered in work, school, leisure, etc.' — a learner here is able to deal with most situations likely to arise while travelling, to produce simple connected text on familiar topics, and to describe experiences and events, dreams, hopes and ambitions, and briefly give reasons and explanations for opinions and plans. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no graded Mongolian word list for learners is published under an open licence, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 71 of the 1000 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — health and the body, the home and the table, money and doing things, the world about us, and describing people and things — and the other 929 are the commonest remaining words of the Mongolian Wikipedia, counted by the WHOLE word: Mongolian adds its case and tense endings to the word (байшин 'house', байшинд 'in the house', байшингаас 'from the house'; явах 'to go', явна 'goes', явсан 'went'), so those forms are added together. That corpus is encyclopaedic, which shows in the fill (history, government, geography). The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words met most often come first. Only words English Wiktionary has an entry for can be taught here, and some common ones are missing from it (хэцүү 'difficult', эсвэл 'or', хэрэв 'if', буцах 'to return'). Every word is in the Cyrillic alphabet, as Mongolian is written in Mongolia, with no romanisation; the Alphabet deck, first in this collection, teaches the letters. A verb is shown by its dictionary form in -х (явах 'to go'). A noun shows its plural and three of its cases where Wiktionary prints its declension table, and a verb its causative and passive where Wiktionary names them; no form is composed here. Example sentences: 96 of the 1000 words have one, from Wiktionary's usage examples and from Tatoeba, which holds about 2,600 Mongolian sentences with a translation; none is invented. There is no speaker button: few devices have a Mongolian voice. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings and forms: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: the Mongolian Wikipedia, articles of the 2026-11-01 dump (CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: English Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0) and Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
